key_insight: Burst restarts in wall turbulence can be explained without assuming pre-existing streak dynamics by tracking how forcing and nonlinear effects rebuild linearly available energy and reorganize vortical structures.
engineering_relevance: This reframes control and modeling of near-wall turbulence by identifying restart mechanisms that may help predict, sustain, or disrupt burst cycles in wall-bounded flows.
method: Study a forced linearised Navier–Stokes system representing nonlinear effects from other structures.
Solve optimisation problems to find minimal conditions that can trigger burst-restart-like responses.
Define linearly available energy (LAE) to quantify the restart process and compare linear-model and real-turbulence patterns.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports qualitative flow-structure analysis from model solutions and real-turbulence restarting stages, showing breakup and merging patterns linked to burst restarts.
watch_item: The framework relies on a reduced forced-linear model, so translating LAE thresholds and restart conditions to complex real flows may require case-specific validation.
paper_title: Restarts of bursts in turbulence in a log-minimal channel
